thread:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: spot-usw2 GPU pool - rapid preemption event. ~45% capacity loss observed. Autoscaler failing to replace nodes due to quota errors. Queue growth > 3x baseline. Paging oncall@maria :rotating_light:

maria: seeing it — thanks. queue spike on request-queue-prod. dashboards show token backlog and request lat p95 climbing. linking metrics: https://dash/redwood/spot-usw2/queue

corey: i'm on logs. cloud provider shows a preemption wave in zone us-west2-b, OCI/GCP spot transitions are frequent. API errors: "QUOTA_EXCEEDED: instance creation disallowed" for the project.

alex: autoscaler repeatedly hitting max-node-limit. config is set to 120 nodes; current desired is 150 but provider refused 30. autoscaler log snippet: ```2026-03-15T18:43:21Z ERROR scaleUp: reached hard-limit```

maria: that's the crux — autoscaler requests aren't being fulfilled, fallback capacity pool didn't attach. we need an immediate mitigation to prevent throttling to customers. Core mitigation options: 1) route traffic to dedicated pools (if capacity) 2) scale down concurrency/batching frontend 3) enable emergency reserve (if legal) 4) customer comms.

jen: i'll take dedicated routing. checking dedicated-usw2 for spare capacity. if we can route non-sensitive tenants there we buy time. also prepping a canary config to reduce max-concurrency to 1 for long-tail jobs.

lee: infra note — reserved GPUs are partially available but quota for the infra project is global and we're near limit. I can request immediate quota bump but provider approval may take minutes-hours. Alternative: spin up smaller VM-backed inference workers w/ slower perf (non-GPU fallback) to drain queue for lowest-priority jobs.

corey: can we temporarily lower batch_size globally to reduce per-request GPU memory? that'll reduce throughput but might keep latency stable for small requests. patch: ```PATCH /config/batching set batch_size=8 -> 4```

maria: do it. reduce batch and reduce max_inflight_requests per-model. jen, initiate routing plan. alex, prepare a manual scaling override to ignore provider errors and mark nodes as 'pending' so autoscaler stops hammering.

alex: manual override ready. command to apply: ```kubectl patch deployment inference-autoscaler -p '{"spec":{"strategy":{"type":"ManualOverride"}}}'``` will stop scale churn. applying now.

ops-bot: Deploy started by alex — inference-autoscaler patch. CI job 7761 running.

maria: alex, confirm patch succeeded and autoscaler isn't making repeat requests.

alex: patch applied. autoscaler paused. now we risk underprovisioning if fallback fails; have to get routing/slow-fallback working asap.

jen: routing check — dedicated-usw2 has ~18% spare. I'll open a canary route for 20% of traffic from low-tiers: ```redwood route create --from request-queue-prod --to dedicated-usw2 --percent 20 --filter 'tier:low'```

ops-bot: Route canary queued. human approval required.

maria: approved. jen proceed. also, set throttles for background batch jobs to zero priority. we want user-facing requests to stay healthy.

ryan: CS standing by. Early signals show ~7% of customers hitting elevated latency; most are low-tier. prepping outbound note: "We're experiencing degraded performance in some regions; working on mitigation." Want me to send now or wait for more stabilization?

maria: send an initial brief — mention impact, mitigation in progress, ETA 30m for next update. avoid technical detail. include how to reach oncall.

ryan: sending now. message posted to status page.

corey: FYI logs show multiple preemption notices with identifier: preempt-evt-20260315-18-43. also noticed that node group tagging prevented fallback-pool attachment due to a label mismatch (label: gpu-type=rtx vs expected nvidia-a100). looks like recent pool onboarding changed labels.

lee: that label mismatch could explain why fallback didn't accept the workload — I'll trigger a quick label sync job to reconcile. command: ```kubectl label nodes -l pool=spot-usw2 gpu-type=a100 --overwrite```

alex: don't mass-label without a check — some nodes are actually T4s. we'll create a selector for a100-only. running a dry-run first.

corey: running quick script to detect real hardware: ```python scripts/inspect_nodes.py --region usw2 --filter 'gpu'``` returns a list; confirming 12 a100, 8 t4.

lee: ok will target a100 nodes only. firing label sync.

ops-bot: label-sync job started (job-id 9924).

maria: good. once labels fixed, autoscaler should be able to attach fallback pool. timeline estimate 6-10 minutes for label job + 3-5 for provider handshake. jen, confirm route traffic change once we see fallback nodes attach.

jen: will watch. also enabling slow-non-gpu nodes to accept low-priority work: ```k8s taint-manager untaint nodegroup=cpu-fallback``` and update priorityClass for batch jobs.

alex: provider replied to a manual ticket: they throttled new instance creation due to a regional maintenance event. they can clear capacity in ~20-30m. request to speed up is submitted.

maria: update on customer impact: front-ends show increased 95th latency in usw2; overall error rate stayed low but server side queueing causing timeouts for some long-running calls. we've prioritized protecting small-latency paths.

ryan: CS posted update noting targeted customers affected and workaround suggestions. customers asking about SLA — I'm tracking escalations.

corey: label-sync completed. fallback pool attached partially. autoscaler resumed with override off, but we set the max surge to prevent overshoot. logs: ```INFO fallback-pool-attach: 8 nodes attached```. queue decreasing but still double baseline.

jen: canary routing live — 20% of low-tier traffic shifted. initial success: latency for canary threads is stable.

maria: good. next steps: 1) watch for provider capacity clearance (20-30m) 2) keep autoscaler capped and batched lowered 3) prepare postmortem notes: root cause likely provider preempt wave + label mismatch + quota limit race 4) follow-up action items: improve label validation, add preempt-drain playbook to runbook, adjust autoscaler backoff and add emergency-reserve pool.

lee: i'll create a quick ticket for label validation and a schedule to reconcile pool labels nightly.

alex: i'll open an autoscaler PR to make the manual override safer and to add exponential backoff when provider returns quota errors.

maria: thanks all. I'll stay on until metrics back to normal. next update in 15m or on milestone change. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident status: mitigations applied. queue decreasing. severity lowered to SEV-2. timeline: incident opened 2865421234, mitigations applied by 2865421488.

ryan: CS update posted: "Mitigations reducing impact, monitoring continued."

maria: closing handoff to eng-sre for follow-up and postmortem. tagging jen/lee/alex/corey. thanks everyone for quick responses.

jen: acknowledged. will take postmortem ownership.

corey: one last note — capture the preempt event IDs and provider ticket for postmortem: preempt-evt-20260315-18-43, provider-ticket-78923.

maria: got it. thread complete for now.
